page.layout: One column of running text. Running head at top centre. Page number at top right. Marginal notes in the right margin: "Ad Simplic." beside line 1, "lib. I. q. 2. & 3." beside lines 2–3, "Enchirid. 96" beside the "potens" line, "De corrupt." beside the "impeditur" line, "& grat. 6." beside the last full line, and "14." at the foot of the right margin. Below the text: catchword "nullam" at right and signature at left.

main_text.l: 8. Citant Augustinum ad Simplicianum. Ve-rum est
(inquit) multi vocati, pauci vero electi. Illi

l.i: enim electi, qui congruenter vocati: illi autem qui
tioni, non electi, quia non secuti, quamvis voca-

main_text.l: ti. Ibid. Igitur non volentis &c. sed miserentis

l.i: Dei, qui hoc modo vocavit, quo modo fit ei congruere

main_text.l: ut vocantem non repuat. Resp. Non negarem
Augustinum (quod res est) ita scripsisse
ante exortam hæresin Pelagianam. Deinde
Augustinus voce congruitatis ideo sæpissime
utitur, quia præoccupare semper illud Pelagij
& humanæ rationis voluit, quo ex omnipo-
tentissima Dei flexione voluntatis liberæ sequi
videtur compelli libertatem & fato cogi,
quod & postea sæpius Pelagiani & Semipela-
giani Augustino objecerunt. Ideo Augustinus o-
mnipotentissimam illam flexionem exposuit
per talem congruitatem moralem, qua Deus
illæsa libertatis natura, ipsam, quo vult, fle-
ctebat, sicut & nos contra Jesuitas & Armi-
nianos cogimur tradere prædeterminationem
talem physicam, quæ tamen locum relinquat
judicio, electioni vitali & indifferentiam
libertatis naturalem, admirando modo, con-
servet, ideoque nostram congruitatem non
Jesuiticam attruit, quippe inspirationes, at-
tractiones omnipotentissimas aperte docuit
Augustinus. Nec ob aliud dicitur veraciter omnipoten-
s, nisi quia quicquid vult, potest, nec voluntate
cujusquam creaturæ voluntatis omnipotentis impe- ditur
effectus. Et idem. Deo volenti salvum facere

page.notes: The transcription treats the whole column as one paragraph, since no indented line starts a new paragraph. The "Ll 5" signature and the "nullam" catchword are read from the foot of the page. The Enchirid. note number and the "& grat. 6." note are partly difficult to read and may be inexact. The marginal "14." at the foot of the right margin is included as a note because it stands in the margin.
